name: Tamozawa Imperial Villa
scope: Standing connected 1899–1921 Tamozawa Imperial Villa including its copper roofs, the raised central three-story residence and open courtyards, in Nikkō.
era: Restored standing villa opened to the public in 2000, represented by its 2018 photographs.

stories.title: Tamozawa Imperial Villa: Three Eras Under One Roof

originalReview.notes: Exact CC0 garden exterior shows the standing succession of dark desaturated copper roofs, deeper three-story central wing, broad eaves and low dark timber verandahs.

originalReview.notes: Exact CC0 view through a circular window shows a low court elevation with raised rails, projecting eaves, timber panels, stone supports and the planting edge. The circular foreground frame is outside scope.

review.method: Exact 2018 Qualla originals, named multi-wing footprint, prefectural heritage record and original GSI elevation
review.notes: Qualla’s exact 2018 garden and court exteriors support present materials and building form. The 74-point mapped roof envelope contains 16 mapped courts and is distinct from the surrounding park. The relation retains a Wikidata/Wikipedia tag for a demolished annex, which is inconsistent with the current site footprint. The prefectural heritage record and the park documentation identify the surviving building.
